explanation: Gateway/NervioSOC data breach activity -- abnormal file read/write volume by a worker process, detected via a rolling 7-day baseline. Confirmed live on real hierarchy 5/101/1/4/1 (2026-08-27): this is the SAME mechanism and tag as the plain breachval flag documented elsewhere for secOpsOutput_105 -- a real product QA test spec confirms the full pipeline. breach.sh reads today's day-of-year, tracks per-day file read/write counts for 3 worker processes in /athinio/security/{1,2,3}_day_N.xml, and once 7 days of data are collected, computes each worker's average read/write count into breach.xml and sets <enable>1. From then on, each day's actual read/write counts are compared against 2x that worker's average -- if EITHER metric for ANY worker is >= 2x its baseline average, <attack>1 is set in breach.xml, a result line is written to /athinio/system/secOpsOutput_105 ('RESULT : Breach attack detected'), and /athinio/system/alertlog.xml's <Breach_val> is set to 1, which rolls up to Alert.xml's breachval tag. Confirmed live: breachval=1 and alertlog.xml's Breach_val=1 on this real hierarchy right now.

known_patterns.meaning: Breach activity detected -- at least one worker's read OR write count on the most recent day was at least double its established baseline average, suggesting abnormal bulk file access (e.g. mass exfiltration or scraping).

evidence_sources.default_meaning: Clean -- the most recent day's read/write counts for all 3 workers stayed below 2x their 7-day rolling average.

metadata.writer_script: breach.sh -> /athinio/system/secOpsOutput_105 + athinio/system/alertlog.xml's Breach_val tag, rolling up to Alert.xml's breachval
metadata.confidence: verified -- confirmed against both a real product QA test spec and live data on a real hierarchy (5/101/1/4/1, 2026-08-27, currently ACTIVE)
metadata.caveat: VERIFICATION CATEGORY DOWNGRADE (2026-08-27): this was originally readable_report, pointing at secOpsOutput_105 and alertlog.xml as 'evidence' -- but both of those are just the SAME <attack> conclusion breach.sh already wrote to Alert.xml's breachval, one file apart, from the exact same script run. Feeding either to an LLM as 'independent verification' is circular: it will almost always just restate what the tag already says, since there's no scenario where they'd disagree except a partial-write bug an LLM isn't well-suited to catch anyway. The genuinely comparable raw numbers (breach.xml's per-worker averages, <filesReadW1> etc.) exist, but the OTHER side of the comparison -- today's actual read/write counts -- lives in /athinio/security/{1,2,3}_day_<today-as-day-of-year>.xml, a dynamically-named file this workflow has no date-arithmetic logic to locate. So even breach.xml alone can't support a real clean-vs-detected judgment. Downgraded to requires_live_recompute to be honest that no real independent verification is currently possible here -- a 'not detected' result is the tag's own claim, unverified, same as ransomware/process_anomaly. Detection only activates once <enable>1 is set in breach.xml, which itself only happens after 7 full days of baseline data have been collected (<started_day> tracks this) -- a freshly-deployed or freshly-reset system will report clean for up to a week before this check is actually live, not because nothing is happening but because there's no baseline yet.
